2. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner getting appointment as Assistant Teacher of Darsona Girls' High School joined the said post on 1-6-1988. His name was duly included in the Monthly Pay Order (MPO). The index number of the petitioner is 2000755. The respondent stopped to pay the Government portion of the salaries since May 1998. It has been stated that the Managing Committee of the said School suspended the petitioner from his service on 22-5-1998. Thereafter on 27-4-1999 the petitioner was dismissed from his service. Challenging the said order of suspension and dismissal dated 22-5-1998 and 27-4-1999 respectively, the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 58/1999 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Darsona, Chuadanga for declaration that the order or suspension and dismissal of the petitioner were illegal, void, collusive and those are not binding upon the petitioner and he is still in service. In the said suit the defendant No. 2, the Headmaster and Member Secretary of Darsona Girls High School appeared and contested the same. After hearing the matter the learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 29th June, 2008 decree the suit declaring the orders of suspension and the dismissal of the petitioner illegal, void, collusive and the Court also declared that the plaintiff petitioner is still in service and directed the defender; of the suit to reinstate the petitioner to his former post. After getting decree, the petitioner joined the School again and he has been realizing the Government portion of the salaries since July, 2008 regularly. The petitioner repeatedly made representations addressing the respondents to get the Government portion of the salaries and other financial benefits from May, 1998 to June, 2008 but the respondents did not take any steps. Lastly the petitioner issued notice demanding justice through his learned Advocate but the respondent did not respond. Then the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr Md Humayun Kabir, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that it is true that the petitioner was dismissed from his service but after recording evidence and considering the statements as made by the School authority the learned Assistant Judge, Darsona, Chuadanga by his judgment and decree dated 19-6-2008 decreed the suit declaring the orders of suspension and the disthissal illegal, void, and collusive and the plaintiff-petitioner is still in service. As the competent Court held that the petitioner is in service so he is entitled to get 'his salaries and other benefits for the aforesaid period. In support of his submission Mr Kabir cited a decision in the case of Md Abdul Haleem vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 3 MLR 105 = 50 DLR 472. 

 5. Mr Md Abdur Rahman Howlader, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the respondent No. 1 submits that as per Nitimala, 1995 the Government is not bound to pay the back salaries of the petition. He further submits that as the learned Assistant Judge in his decree did not direct to pay the Government portion of the salary so the petitioner is not entitled to get any back salaries and other benefits. 

 7. There is no dispute that the petitioner, getting appointment as Assistant Teacher of Darsona High School, joined the said School on 1-6-1988 and he had been serving till the date of his dismissal. His name was duly included in the Monthly Pay Order and he used to release the Government portion of the salaries till stoppage of payment. Then challenging his orders of suspension and dismissal the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 58/1999 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Darsona, Chuadanga and got the contested decree (Annexure-D to the writ petition). It appears from the said decree that the learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit declaring the order of dismissal collusive and the same was not binding upon the petitioner and also declared that the petitioner is still in service. As the competent Court of law declared that the plaintiff-petitioner is still in service setting aside the order of dismissal so he is entitled to get salaries for the period of his suspension and dismissal.
